main_text.p: conficiendi commeatuum copia summo studio curavit. Occupata ab eo tyrannis est Olympiadis cxv anno quarto, qui fuit post relegatum in Græciam Dionysium, & reparatæ libertatis initium vicesimus sextus. Post quæ idem Agathocles varia bella gessit, primum in Sicilia contra exules Syracusanos, Agrigentinos, Gelaos, Messanenses, & hostes gravissimos & potentissimos Pœnos: deinde ut armorum Punicorum mala ex patria in terram hostilem transferret, anno dominatus sui vii, qui erat Olympiadis cxvii annus tertius, omnibus domi contra motus intestini pericula constitutis, cum exercitu in Africam trajecit, & vario successu bello illic administrato, demum relicto ibi filio natu maximo Archagatho ad continuandum bellum, ipse in Siciliam rediit, & multis ibidem casibus jactatus ob adversam filii fortunam denuo in Africam profectus, sed & ipse deteriore quàm ante fortuna usus, defertis duobus filiis cum exercitu furtim in Siciliam se recepit, exacto post primum in Africam adventum anno quarto. Dein cognita filiorum suorum nece, quos ira-milites in Africà occiderant, in ra-iem[?] versus, composita, ut poterat, cum Pœnis pace, in omne genus crudelitatis se

page.notes: Printed text runs to the foot of the page and ends mid-sentence with the catchword "fe". The page opens mid-sentence, so the first paragraph continues from the previous page. Doubtful readings: "ira-milites" (hyphenated line end; the word may be "iratis" or another form) and "ra-iem" (the reading "ratiem" is not Latin, so the intended word is uncertain). The reading "cxvii" for the Olympiad numeral is uncertain. The long s is rendered as plain s throughout, so "poft" appears as "post" and "eft" as "est". A small asterisk stands at the bottom left, outside the text block. It is not a gathering signature and is not transcribed. Left and bottom edges show fragments of the neighbouring page, which are omitted.
